speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the emergency room. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; have you noticed any specific symptoms like grunting, nasal flaring, or chest retractions since birth? Please tell me if there was any history of meconium aspiration or prolonged rupture of membranes.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; given the prematurity and gestational diabetes, we need to assess the severity of the distress. Can you tell me if the baby is currently requiring oxygen support and what their heart rate and oxygen saturation levels are? REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas, Pulse_Oximetry.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Oxygen_Saturation: 88% on room air, improving with oxygen; Heart_Rate: 104/min; Blood_Gas_Analysis: pH 7.30, PaCO2 50 mm Hg, PaO2 60 mm Hg, HCO3- 24 mEq/L, Base_Excess -5

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
